name: Runta

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: RAM allocation may autoscale. Fixed requested 8 GiB is used in the example; actual resized RAM changes charges.

plans.name: Prepaid
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

caveats: Public list rates. Prepaid billing with $5 minimum manual top-up, no subscription. Paused/suspended/shut-down runtime retains billed disk. Memory auto scaling can change the billed allocation; do not confuse that with active CPU billing.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.
SSH: docs overview lists an SSH gateway ("the stable SSH gateway host key") and attaching SSH keys to runtimes -> ssh true (verified 2026-09-28).

Desktop: runtimes expose a VNC desktop ("Enable the runtime VNC desktop"; Cloud Agent computer sessions = "runtime's desktop through VNC over WebSocket") -> desktop true. No bundled browser or computer-use (screenshot/mouse) API is documented: browser and computer_use stay null (unverified).
Snapshot/checkpoint storage and egress prices are not published (pricing page + checkpoints + egress docs re-checked 2026-09-28): snapshot_gib_month and egress_gib stay null (unknown, not free).
Free trial accounts share limits of 32 vCPU and 64 GiB memory (pricing page); paid-account limits unpublished.
Runtime disk is 16-256 GiB (API minimum 16 GiB), so every runtime pays at least 16 GiB at the disk rate.

Auto-suspend (preview): idle threshold from 1 s, but the scan runs every 60 s, so suspension can happen ~1 scan after the threshold (a 30 s timeout can take ~90 s) and that tail is billed. Checkpoint restore creates a new runtime.

fleet.verification: Free trial no card; adding payment method unlocks higher resources. Minimum prepaid top-up $5; automatic refills opt-in.
fleet.tiers: Free aggregate 32 vCPU and 64 GiB across runtimes; higher paid limits not numerically stated.
fleet.notes: At 4 vCPU/8 GiB this bounds trial at 8; no published 10/50/300/1,000 guaranteed paid fleet quota. Numeric instance/GPU count and manual increase route unknown.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote:
Send another request to wake the runtime. The wake-up path restores the runtime
and then proxies the original request:
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in, preview: idle_policy suspend_only or suspend_and_wakeup (default disabled) suspends a runtime after N s without inbound HTTP traffic (scan every 60 s) and restores it on the next request / explicit start. Pricing bills suspended runtimes for 'Disk storage only', so state is saved off the host RAM; whether running processes (memory) survive suspend is not stated explicitly.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A checkpoint is a point-in-time capture of a runtime’s state, including filesystem and running processes.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included (kind full/live = 'Full VM snapshot'; cold = disk-only of a shut-down runtime, per openapi.yaml CreateCheckpointRequest). 'Restoring a checkpoint creates a new runtime', so one checkpoint can seed many runtimes (fork); Cloud Agents can also be created from a checkpoint. Checkpoint storage price unpublished.

harness_api.quote:
By default, each new Cloud Agent gets its own Runta runtime with one managed Pi
agent instance. Send a prompt through the REST API, watch the agent work, and
collect its reply or files.
harness_api.note: Pi only: 'Cloud Agents currently use Pi RPC. The harness.kind field does not select Codex CLI or Claude Code.' REST /v2/agents: create agent, POST runs (prompt + images), SSE event stream with reconnect cursor, follow-ups (steer active run), resume, cancel, list runs, sessions kept across runs, workspace files and artifacts, VNC computer sessions. Several harnesses can share one runtime. Model via managed provider (OpenAI/Anthropic/Kimi/compatible API or a connected Codex subscription). Exo Harness is also offered as a built-in runtime image, driven via web terminal (no separate API documented).

egress_allowlist.quote: Policy entries are hostnames or wildcard host patterns, not URLs:
egress_allowlist.note: Per-runtime allowlist or denylist mode (default = empty denylist, i.e. open), set via CLI/SDK/API and replaceable on a running runtime; enforced by Runta's egress gateway. No IP/CIDR or port rules documented.

ingress_rules.quote:
Runta can make your agent publicly accessible.
Each runtime can publish up to 16 ports.
ingress_rules.note: Only ports you list in ingress_specs (http/https, up to 16) are published at https://<port>-<runtime_id>.runta.dev; nothing is exposed by default. Published ports are public: no auth token, private mode or IP allowlist documented. Image web UIs (e.g. desktop) are 'published through the runtime's ingress on demand, behind a session gateway' (openapi.yaml); VNC uses expiring credentials.

secret_proxy.quote:
Secret stubs match a destination host and optional path. The literal
${credential} placeholder is replaced with the stored secret value when the
egress gateway injects the outbound request.
secret_proxy.note: 'Runta can authenticate your agent’s request without exposing real credentials to your agents.' Arbitrary host + path pattern, header + template (e.g. Bearer ${credential}); tenant secret store with cache TTL. Also used for Cloud Agent model providers and Codex subscription tokens ('the guest receives neither the real token nor a Codex credential file'). Only HTTP header injection documented; no DB/SSH/git-over-SSH.

volume_attach.note: The full public OpenAPI contract (runtimes, checkpoints, secrets, images, files, agents) has no volume resource; storage is the runtime's own disk (16-256 GiB, resizable disk_gib). Not explicitly denied in prose.

volume_shared.note: No shared volume / network filesystem / bucket mount in the API. Multiple Cloud Agent harnesses can share one runtime (same computer), which is not a shared volume.

browser.quote: The runtime supplies the computer, browser, filesystem, and model routing; the agent instance maintains its conversation.
browser.note: A managed browser is part of the Cloud Agent runtime's computer, viewable/controllable through the VNC computer session.

anti_bot.quote: Runta is an execution layer for AI agents. It provides scalable, governed runtimes with strong control over state, access, credentials, and execution.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Runta positions itself as a governed agent execution/runtime layer (compute, egress control, secrets, checkpoints), not a stealth/anti-fingerprinting browsing service; no stealth or fingerprint-evasion feature is documented anywhere.

captcha_solving.quote: Runta is an execution layer for AI agents. It provides scalable, governed runtimes with strong control over state, access, credentials, and execution.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving capability is documented in any Runta docs, CLI, SDK, or REST API reference.

fork_running.quote: Full VM snapshot (`full` or equivalent `live`), or disk-only snapshot (`cold`) of a fully shutdown runtime.
fork_running.note: Only the `cold` checkpoint kind requires the runtime to be fully shut down; `full`/`live` checkpoints (which include running processes, per the checkpoints doc) are taken from a runtime without shutting it down, and restoring any checkpoint creates a new independent runtime — i.e. cloning a running machine without stopping it.

own_agent_api.quote: By default, each new Cloud Agent gets its own Runta runtime with one managed Pi agent instance. Send a prompt through the REST API, watch the agent work, and collect its reply or files. The runtime supplies the computer, browser, filesystem, and model routing.
own_agent_api.note: The Cloud Agents REST API drives Runta's own managed 'Pi' agent (prompts, runs, follow-ups, streamed events, computer/browser sessions, workspace/artifacts) — Runta's own task/computer-use agent, not a bring-your-own coding harness.

mcp_server.quote: Runta REST API ... CLI Reference ... SDK Reference
mcp_server.note: The full docs sidebar lists CLI, Python SDK, TypeScript SDK, and REST API references but no MCP server; no MCP mention found anywhere on runta.com or its GitHub org.

public_ipv4.quote:
Runta can make your agent publicly accessible.
Each runtime can publish up to 16 ports.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is via published HTTPS ports at a Runta-managed subdomain (https://<port>-<runtime_id>.runta.dev) through a gateway, not a per-machine public IPv4 address; no public IPv4 offering is documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Runta is an execution layer for AI agents. It provides scalable, governed runtimes with strong control over state, access, credentials, and execution.
guest_firewall.note: derived: runtimes are isolated VMs with SSH access and Docker-inside support, which typically implies guest-level root/sudo access sufficient to run iptables/nftables; not independently confirmed by Runta docs.

static_egress_ip.quote: Policy entries are hostnames or wildcard host patterns, not URLs
static_egress_ip.note: Egress control is a per-runtime hostname allow/deny-list gateway; no dedicated/fixed outbound IP address feature is documented.

gpu.quote: Resource rates ... vCPU $0.0504 vCPU-hour Memory $0.0162 GiB-hour Disk storage $0.000108 GiB-hour
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — pricing only meters vCPU, memory, and disk; no GPU meter, GPU instance type, or GPU mention exists anywhere on the site or in openapi.yaml.

windows.quote: A Runta runtime is an isolated computer where AI agents can work, persist state, and access external resources—with observability and control built in.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — runtimes are created from Linux Runtime Images (Dockerfile-based custom images), exec examples use sh/bash, and no Windows machine option is documented.

macos.quote: A Runta runtime is an isolated computer where AI agents can work, persist state, and access external resources—with observability and control built in.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS machine type is documented; runtimes are Linux VMs built from Dockerfile-based Runtime Images.

self_host.quote: Runta is an execution layer for AI agents. It provides scalable, governed runtimes with strong control over state, access, credentials, and execution.
self_host.note: Runta is offered only as a hosted SaaS (api.runta.com) with usage-based billing; no self-hosted/on-prem deployment option is documented.

byoc.quote: Runta is an execution layer for AI agents. It provides scalable, governed runtimes with strong control over state, access, credentials, and execution.
byoc.note: No bring-your-own-cloud / deploy-into-your-account offering is documented; the product is accessed exclusively via Runta's own hosted API.

open_source.quote: errand: An open-source take on Grok Bot/Muse. Persistent AI teammates with their own cloud computers, powered by Runta.
open_source.note: Runta's GitHub org (runta-dev) publishes open-source side projects (errand, clawshell, a codex fork) built on top of Runta, but the core Runta execution layer/runtime platform itself is closed-source hosted infrastructure.

soc2.note: SOC 2 Type II is explicitly listed as 'in progress', not yet attested, on Runta's Trust Center.

hipaa.note: Runta's Trust Center lists only SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 (both in progress) as frameworks; no HIPAA eligibility or BAA is mentioned anywhere.

sso.quote: Team Access and Roles Manage members from Settings → Team access with Owner, Admin, and Developer roles.
sso.note: Team access is documented only as simple role-based access (Owner/Admin/Developer); no SAML/OIDC single sign-on is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: Create a Runtime ... runta run --name demo --cpus 2 --memory 2048
eu_data_residency.note: No region selection appears anywhere in the CLI/SDK/REST API (create-runtime has no region parameter in openapi.yaml) or docs, implying a single deployment region rather than a choice of EU residency.

max_session_h.quote: Lifecycle calls change runtime state without deleting the runtime record, except for delete, which permanently removes it.
max_session_h.note: Runtimes are long-lived VMs controlled by explicit boot/pause/resume/shutdown/delete calls (plus opt-in auto-suspend on idle); no maximum session duration is published anywhere in pricing or docs.

egress_ip_type.quote: Runta can control which external services your agent can access.
egress_ip_type.note: Runta's egress feature is a per-runtime hostname allow/deny-list gateway for outbound traffic control; no residential, mobile, or ISP-proxy IP product is documented anywhere on the site, blog, or API. Runta positions itself as a governed agent execution/compute layer (standard cloud VM egress), not a proxy/anti-bot network, so outbound IPs are inferred to be ordinary datacenter IPs rather than residential/mobile; no explicit 'datacenter IP' statement was found.

arm64.quote: architectures: type: array items: type: string enum: - x86_64 - aarch64 ... CreateRuntimeImageBuildRequest ... architecture: type: string enum: - x86_64 default: x86_64
arm64.note: The generic RuntimeImage schema declares 'aarch64' as a theoretically allowed value for an image's architectures field, but the only concrete example response shows architectures: ["x86_64"], and the endpoint for building your own custom Runtime Image from a Dockerfile (CreateRuntimeImageBuildRequest, and the separate RuntimeImageBuild.architecture field) restricts architecture to the single enum value x86_64. No aarch64/ARM runtime image, size, or pricing is advertised anywhere on runta.com. Treated as not currently offered.
